To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) MDL and MTL are unified by a semantic descriptor, (2) the semantic descriptor can be encoded in different ways, (3) the semantic descriptor enables zero-shot learning and domain adaptation, (4) the semantic descriptor provides a unified framework for multi-linear algebra and neural networks, and (5) the semantic descriptor is a key to a generalisation of MTL to MDL and ZSL.

(1) the semantic descriptor is a key concept for understanding the relationship between multi-domain and multi-task learning; (2) the framework is general enough to encompass various existing MDL and MTL algorithms; (3) the framework can be generalised to a higher order form that is mathematically equivalent to gated neural networks, providing a novel neural architecture for zero-shot learning and zero-shot domain adaptation
